gate.reason: Human re-ruling 09-03 (interactive): the first ruling — refuse a duplicate member address within a kind — was built (e4ff7bc6) and failed temper's own self-host test at afterMerge: Claude Code allows N matcher groups per event and this repo's own harness carries two PostToolUse groups, so a duplicate-event refusal rejects every real harness. The defect (silent last-writer-wins on edge resolution to `hook:<Event>`) stands; the remedy is a hook identity discriminator, which is a model fork, not build's to invent.

edit.description: New sibling check beside `collection_address_collision_diagnostics` (which 21f61463 added for two *kinds* sharing one collectionAddress): a *single* kind's own members registering on the same key within that address (e.g. three `hook` members on `SessionStart`, which collapse to one entry in the `kind:name` composition map — silent last-writer-wins) is a declaration-time refusal with a named error, not a silent collapse.
Wire the new diagnostic beside the existing `collection_address_collision_diagnostics` call (~gate.rs:200s).
Regression: three hook members declared on the same event refuse loud, naming all colliding members — mirroring 21f61463's kind-collision test shape.

summary: Refuse a duplicate member registration key within one kind's collection address (three hooks on SessionStart collapse to one) with a named error, not last-writer-wins.

tests.asserts: duplicate hook members on the same event name are refused loud, naming both

acceptance: Two `hook` members declared on the same `event` refuse at declaration time with a named error rather than silently composing to whichever was last.
